newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tribal refugees may return from India.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tribal refugees may return from India.

text.p: Bangladeshi tribal refugees who fled to India to escape insurgency in the Chittagong Hill Tracts are expected to start returning home later this month, government officials said on Friday.
They said the repatriation was likely to begin soon after a Bangladesh government team, led by parliamentarian Abul Hasanat Abdullah, visited refugee camps in the northeast Indian state of Tripura.
A statement issued by Abdullah's office on Thursday said he would leave for Tripura, bordering Bangladesh, on February 27 for talks with the refugee leaders.
Abdullah is chairman of a national committee trying to restore peace in the Hill Tracts, home to 13 tribes and some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers.
Government and leaders of the rebel Shanti Bahini guerrillas held their first meeting in Dhaka late last month but failed to reach any deal to halt the revolt.
They agreed to meet again on March 12.
The Shanti Bahini, made up mostly of Chakma tribesmen, has fought since 1973 for autonomy for the 5,500-sq-mile (14,200-sq-km) Hill Tracts, which border India and Burma.
The rebels accuse the settlers of stealing their land and destroying their culture. They want them expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which has forced about 50,000 tribespeople to seek refuge in India.
Some 6,000 refugees were repatriated in 1994, but the process was stopped for unexplained reasons.
